What the numbers say

For the session of Monday, October 12, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (26 US-listed stocks and ETFs on DappGo's reviewed watchlist) as risk-on. SPY is above its 50-day average and above its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is up and realised volatility is in the calm band.

17 of 26 tickers (65%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 16 of 25 (64%) above their 200-day average. Above 55% is the breadth the model requires, together with the benchmark above its 50-day average and volatility not high, for a risk-on reading. On the day 12 rose and 14 fell; the median move was −0.06%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Communication had the strongest average move at +1.47% and Technology the weakest at −1.63%, a spread of 3.10 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 1.03 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

No ticker has a 14-day RSI at or below 30, and 1 at or above 70 (SHEL). An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.
